questions.question: Discuss applications of predictive analytics
questions.solution_html:
• Predictive analytics uses historical data and statistical models to forecast future outcomes or
  • trends. It identifies patterns and probabilities to make educated guesses about what might
  • happen.
  • • Applications
  • o Finance: Fraud detection and credit risk assessment.
  • o Marketing: Predicting customer churn and creating personalized product
  • recommendations.
  • o Operations: Inventory forecasting and predictive maintenance (to anticipate
  • equipment failure).

questions.question: Demonstrate how data anonymization can protect sensitive information / during analysis?
questions.solution_html:
• Demonstrate how data anonymization can protect sensitive information
  • during analysis?
  • Data anonymization is an ethical consideration in data analytics used to protect privacy by
  • ensuring individuals cannot be identified from the data.
  • Techniques
  • Masking/Encryption: Replacing sensitive identifying fields (like names or IDs) with fake or
  • encrypted values.
  • Generalization: Replacing specific values with a broader category (e.g., replacing a specific
  • age with an age range like '20-30').
  • Swapping: Exchanging attributes between different records, which maintains the overall
  • statistical properties but breaks the link to specific individuals.
  • Protection: By removing or obscuring personally identifiable information (PII)
  • anonymization allows for data to be used for manipulation and analysis without violating
  • privacy regulations.

questions.question: / detection, credit risk assessment, and investment forecasting.
questions.solution_html:
• detection, credit risk assessment, and investment forecasting.
  • These are industry-specific applications (finance) that utilize data analytics.
  • • Fraud Detection: Analyzes transaction data in real-time using algorithms to identify

  • • Investment Forecasting: Employs advanced techniques like time-series analysis and
  • machine learning to predict stock price movements, market trends, and asset volatility
  • guiding strategic investment decisions.

questions.question: Describe importance of Data Transformation in data analysis.
questions.solution_html:
• Data transformation is the process of converting data from one format or structure to another
  • often involving steps like Data Cleaning.
  • Importance
  • o Compatibility: Ensures the data is in the correct format for the specific
  • analytical tools or algorithms being used.
  • o Data Quality: Improves quality by reducing inconsistencies, redundancies, and
  • improving overall accuracy.
  • o Normalization/Scaling: Ensures all variables are on a similar scale, preventing
  • features with larger values from dominating the analysis.
  • o Feature Engineering: Creates new, more insightful variables (features) from the
  • existing data, which significantly improves the performance of predictive
  • models.

questions.question: Explain the significance of outliers / Show with examples how structured, semi-structured, and unstructured
questions.solution_html:
• Outliers are observations that lie an abnormal distance from other values in a random sample
  • from a population (Handling Missing Data and Outliers).
  • Significance
  • o Data Errors: Often, they indicate genuine data entry errors or measurement
  • mistakes that must be cleaned or removed for accurate analysis.
  • o Valuable Insight: Sometimes, outliers represent rare but significant events (e.g.
  • a major system failure, a highly profitable anomaly, or fraud) that are critical to
  • the analysis.
  • o Model Distortion: If left unhandled, outliers can severely skew statistical results
  • (like the mean and standard deviation) and reduce the reliability and accuracy
  • of analytical models.

questions.question: / formats appear in everyday life.
questions.solution_html:
• Show with examples how structured, semi-structured, and unstructured
  • formats appear in everyday life.
  • • Structured Data: Highly organized data that fits into a fixed schema (rows and
  • columns).
  • o Example: A Spreadsheet or database table containing employee records with
  • fixed fields for Employee ID, Name, and Date of Hire.
  • • Semi-structured Data: Data that has organizational tags or markers but does not
  • conform to a formal table structure.
  • o Example: An email (has structured "To," "From," and "Date" fields, but the
  • body content is free-form) or a JSON/XML file.
  • • Unstructured Data: Data with no predefined structure, often text or media based.
  • o Example: The full body text of a news article, a photograph or video file, or
  • the content of a social media post.
